passages.heading: Orange County Democrats are standing with Roberta.
passages.text: Democratic leaders from across Orange County came together to deliver a clear message: this election should be about character, qualifications, experience, integrity, and who is truly prepared to lead the Clerk of Court on Day One.

passages.heading: Orange County Democrats are standing with Roberta.
passages.text: State Senator LaVon Bracy Davis — who has known Roberta for more than two decades, and who made history alongside her in the inaugural graduating class of the re-established Florida A&M University College of Law — spoke to the dignity and strength Roberta has shown throughout this campaign.

passages.heading: Orange County Democrats are standing with Roberta.
passages.text: “Pressure doesn’t create character. Pressure reveals it.” “While voters can’t object, they can reject.”

passages.heading: Orange County Democrats are standing with Roberta.
passages.text: Senator Bracy Davis was joined by Congressman Maxwell Alejandro Frost, Senator Carlos Guillermo Smith, Representative Anna V. Eskamani, Representative RaShon Young, and other Democratic leaders calling for a campaign focused on qualifications, experience, and readiness to serve.

passages.heading: The first face of justice for our community.
passages.text: The Clerk's Office is more than a government office. It is the heartbeat of our local justice system. For many residents, the Clerk's Office is the very first face of justice they encounter during some of the most important, emotional, and life-changing moments of their lives.

passages.heading: The first face of justice for our community.
passages.text: The Clerk's Office is responsible for protecting court records, supporting our justice partners, managing the court registry, and ensuring all residents have meaningful access to justice.

passages.heading: A campaign built on service, not slogans.
passages.text: Roberta is running to ensure the office remains grounded in professionalism, accessibility, innovation, accountability, and trusted leadership, with the competence, compassion, and clear understanding of how the Clerk's Office impacts the daily lives of Orange County residents.

passages.heading: Access to Justice
passages.text: Every resident deserves dignity, respect, professionalism, and compassion when they interact with the Clerk's Office.

passages.heading: Modern Technology
passages.text: Innovate and rebrand our offices as a technology-forward service provider built for our growing population.

passages.heading: Public Records Integrity
passages.text: Safeguard official court records, protect public funds, and uphold the highest standard of data quality.

passages.heading: Community & Court Connection
passages.text: Build community education partnerships that strengthen public trust and help residents navigate the courts.

passages.heading: A legal career built in service of Orange County.
passages.text: From legal aid to General Counsel for the Clerk of Court, Roberta has spent her career making the justice system work for the people who depend on it. The cards on the right cycle through the milestones see the full picture for the details behind each chapter.

passages.heading: Attorney, Access to Justice
passages.text: Community Legal Services of Mid-Florida, Inc.

passages.heading: What does the Clerk of Court actually do?
passages.text: Most residents never hear about the Clerk of Court until they need it. Roberta takes the time to explain the office in plain language — what it handles, how it protects your records, and why it matters to every family in Orange County.

passages.heading: What does the Clerk of Court actually do?
passages.text: Watch the full video series to learn how the office works and what experienced leadership looks like.

passages.heading: Your Connection to the Courts
passages.text: Bridging Justice and Community, a platform built on professionalism, accessibility, innovation, and accountability.

passages.heading: Expand Access to Court and Prioritize the Customer Experience
passages.text: Every person who interacts with the Clerk's Office should be treated with dignity, respect, and professionalism. Roberta will lead a customer-centered Clerk's Office that meets people where they are and removes barriers to accessing the courts.

passages.heading: Improve Efficiency and Modern Technology Solutions
passages.text: Orange County is growing, and the Clerk's Office must grow with it. Roberta will champion innovation and technology-forward service so the office is efficient today and prepared for the needs of tomorrow.

passages.heading: Protect the Integrity of Public Records and the Quality of Court Data
passages.text: The Clerk is the official keeper of the court's records and the steward of public funds. Roberta will safeguard court records, protect public dollars, and uphold the data quality that the public, the bar, and the bench rely on.

passages.heading: Connect the Community and the Courts through Civic Engagement & Court Literacy
passages.text: Roberta will lead community education partnerships that help residents understand how their courts work for them, building public trust between the Clerk's Office and every neighborhood it serves.

passages.heading: Meet Roberta Walton Johnson, Esq.
passages.text: General Counsel for the Orange County Clerk of Circuit and County Courts, FAMU College of Law graduate, and lifelong public servant, running to be your next Orange County Clerk of Court.

passages.heading: A legal career grounded in public service.
passages.text: Roberta Walton Johnson serves as General Counsel for the Orange County Clerk of Circuit and County Courts, where she provides strategic legal guidance, advances legislative and policy initiatives, and supports the Clerk's mission of innovation, accessibility, accountability, and public service.

passages.heading: A legal career grounded in public service.
passages.text: Since joining the Clerk's Office in 2015, Roberta has played a key leadership role in strengthening public access to the justice system. She established and led the Lydia Gardner Self Help Center, helping expand meaningful access to justice for self-represented litigants and families throughout Orange County. Her work has focused on ensuring that residents can navigate the court system with dignity, professionalism, and support.

passages.heading: A legal career grounded in public service.
passages.text: A proud graduate of Florida A&M University and the reestablished Florida A&M University College of Law, Roberta earned her Juris Doctor in 2005 as a member of the inaugural graduating class. Her legal career has been rooted in service from the very beginning. Following law school, she joined Community Legal Services of Mid-Florida, where she represented and advocated for low-income and underserved residents in critical legal matters.

passages.heading: A legal career grounded in public service.
passages.text: Her broad professional experience includes public sector leadership with Orange County Government, private practice experience with Voight P.A., and years of nonprofit leadership directing community-based programs and initiatives throughout Florida's Big Bend region. This unique combination of legal, governmental, nonprofit, and operational experience has prepared Roberta to lead the Clerk's Office with competence, vision, and integrity from Day One.

passages.heading: Building the Lydia Gardner Self Help Center.
passages.text: Roberta established and led the Lydia Gardner Self Help Center, the front door for residents who need to navigate Orange County's courts without an attorney. Under her leadership, the Center became a model for accessible, dignified, customer-centered court service.

passages.heading: A Florida A&M Rattler, twice over.
passages.text: "There is no substitute for experience. When it comes to protecting our courts, serving our community, and leading on Day One, experience matters."

passages.heading: Rooted in Orange County.
passages.text: While her professional accomplishments and community leadership are extensive, Roberta considers her greatest blessing to be her family. She is married to Neil Johnson and is the proud mother of two sons, Dakari and Dylan.
